newsitem.title: USA: Glendale Federal sets Transworld purchase.
newsitem.headline: Glendale Federal sets Transworld purchase.

text.p: Glendale Federal Bank said it agreed to acquire TransWorld Bancorp in a cash transaction valued at $63.0 million.

Under the terms of the agreement, Glendale Federal said, it will pay $18.25 each for TransWorld common share, equivalent to 1.96 times TransWorld's book value on September 30. The agreement is subject to regulatory and other approvals and is expected to close early in the second calendar quarter of 1997.

The acquisition would enhance Glendale Federal's business banking focus by bringing significant new business banking capabilities, including small business relationship building experience and Small Business Administration lending expertise, said Glendale Federal.

In addition, TransWorld is a strong generator of business-related deposits and Glendale Federal will benefit from the addition of branches which are located in communities where we would like to have a stronger presence.

Founded in 1953 and headquartered in Sherman Oaks, TransWorld Bank is a state-chartered commercial bank specializing in small business lending and is one of the California's largest SBA lenders. At September 30, it had assets of $375.3 million, deposits of $337.8 million and loans of $136.4 million. About 73 percent of its deposits are in daily access accounts and 79 percent of its loans are to businesses. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610
